moved.sentence: Treat a remote MCP server as an OAuth 2.1 **resource server**.

judged.note: Treating a remote MCP server as an OAuth 2.1 resource server is kept, the unkeyed instruction at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: To call a downstream service, use a token-exchange flow to obtain a distinct token, or act as its own client.

judged.note: Using token exchange for a distinct downstream token, or acting as its own client, is kept at SHOULD; the passthrough ban stays MUST NOT in must-not-pass-tokens-through.

moved.sentence: When the server proxies a third-party API using a static client ID, a stale consent cookie lets an attacker skip the consent screen.

judged.note: The confused-deputy threat (static client ID proxy, stale consent cookie skipping consent) is kept in rationale as the reason for the per-client consent rules.

moved.sentence: Treat every string the server emits as model-influencing input and every token it receives as untrusted.

judged.note: Treating every emitted string as model-influencing input and every received token as untrusted is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Pin guidance to the MCP spec revision dated **2025-06-18** (Security Best Practices + Authorization), which carries the normative MUST/MUST NOT statements below.

judged.note: Pinning to the MCP spec revision 2025-06-18 (Security Best Practices + Authorization) is kept at SHOULD with its note about the normative statements.

moved.sentence: A server (or a tool it proxies) can present a benign description at approval time and a malicious one later.

judged.note: The rug-pull threat, benign description at approval and malicious later, is kept in rationale for the hash-binding and versioning rules.

moved.sentence: They **SHOULD** require HTTPS (loopback excepted for dev), block private/reserved ranges (`10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`, `169.254/16`, `127/8`, `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10`), and validate redirect targets per hop.

judged.note: Server-side deployments requiring HTTPS (loopback dev exception), blocking the same private/reserved ranges and validating redirects per hop are kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Prefer an egress proxy and DNS-pinning over hand-rolled IP parsing, which misses octal/hex/IPv4-mapped-IPv6 encodings.

judged.note: Preferring an egress proxy and DNS-pinning over hand-rolled IP parsing, with the octal/hex/IPv4-mapped-IPv6 reason, is kept at SHOULD.
